topic: Code as an Artifact: Versioning AI-Generated Code

key_points: Agentic LLMs have changed what 'code' means — it used to be the end product of the software lifecycle, but now LLMs write code and the spec becomes the durable artifact
Elon Musk's argument: source code is becoming like assembly; the next step is generating efficient binaries directly with AI
Counter-argument: if you move programming into LLMs, your instructions/prompt and context become the 'code' — one higher level of abstraction, but still code
Programming languages won't disappear because they reduce ambiguity in natural-language specification; they exist to make execution unambiguous
LLMs can trivially generate binaries, but what you assert the binary will do still depends on 'code' at a higher level
Build a line-aware, Git-native provenance system with a dual-layer data model: attribution map (fast blame path) + exchange records (explainability path)
Back with always-on micro-versioning (journal + checkpoints) and a deterministic correlation engine
Design goals: answer 'who changed this line, AI or human, and why?', preserve causality before commit flattening, survive branch/merge/rebase/squash/cherry-pick
Hybrid capture stack: explicit agent hooks + provider watchers/parsers, normalized into one ExchangeEvent schema
Scored deterministic matcher over path match, content hash continuity, time-window proximity, session affinity, change-type compatibility
The bottleneck isn't writing code anymore — it's trusting it; AI code generation speed has surpassed human review capacity
Humans never truly scaled code review: reviewers overloaded with backlogs approve PRs with critical bugs, often focusing on style
Code review (human or LLM) was not designed for autonomous coding — it doesn't verify the code accomplishes what was prompted or aligns with spec
Even 5-axes best practices (correctness, architecture, security, readability, performance) fall short of verifying original acceptance criteria
LLM-written code is an artifact of the process that created it — reviewing only the generated artifact misses the context of how it was produced
The missing piece: plans, prompting, and the full dialog behind a change; PR summaries don't capture tradeoffs and alternatives
If natural language (prompting/planning) is the new 'programming language', only putting the generated code up for review is incomplete
Open question: how to review PRs given this disconnect — what rules/automation to institute
Backwards Build: start with business slides → PRD → documentation → tests → THEN code; generate code only after product makes human sense
Leverage MCP to connect AI with codebases, docs, and external tools in a standardized way
Standardize aggressively: minimal invention, strong typing, follow existing conventions; strict linting with no exceptions
Verification gates: require AI to produce tests, docs, and diagrams with mandatory human review before proceeding
Size limits (50 lines/function, 200 lines/file), keep the whole chain in sync daily, human-AI joint code reviews

stats.fact: Elon Musk (Aug 2026): 'Source code is on the verge of becoming like assembly. The next step is getting rid of source code entirely and just making an efficient binary directly with AI.'
A 6-month-old startup with a 300k-line Next.js monorepo runs 3-6 AI coding agents in parallel across git worktrees, with 0 traditional SWE backgrounds among founders.
The startup enforces a four-phase pipeline (discussion → plan → implement → review) with custom Claude Code slash commands, scoring every plan 1-10 for one-pass implementation confidence.
Git-native provenance systems (SpecStory) recommend a dual-layer model: attribution map in Git Notes for fast blame + exchange records for explainability, backed by always-on micro-versioning.
The bottleneck in software engineering has shifted from writing code to trusting it — AI generation speed has surpassed human review capacity.

angles: The paradigm shift: code is no longer the end product — the spec/prompt/context is the durable artifact, and code is a regenerable output
Why traditional Git is insufficient for AI-generated code: it captures the artifact but not the process (prompts, plans, agent context) that produced it
Provenance as the new requirement: line-level attribution of 'who changed this, AI or human, and why'
The review bottleneck: humans never scaled code review, and AI code makes it worse — need new verification gates
Practical workflow patterns: backwards build, verification gates, size limits, human-AI joint review, plan scoring
Tooling landscape: Git Notes-based provenance, micro-versioning, agent trace standards (C2PA, SLSA, in-toto, OpenTelemetry GenAI semconv)
